_about: SEIFA (ABS Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas) per federal electoral division, all four indexes: IRSD = Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (pure disadvantage; HIGH score = LESS disadvantaged), IER = Index of Economic Resources, IEO = Index of Education and Occupation, IRSAD = Index of Relative Socio-Economic Advantage and Disadvantage. irsd/ier/ieo ranks run 1 = MOST disadvantaged (the APH tapes' own order); an irsad cell instead carries TWO ranks — `rank` = 1 most ADVANTAGED (the sibling pipeline's and the index's natural read), `rankDis` = 1 most disadvantaged (this store's convention, = N+1-rank). Every index cell ALSO carries pct, its within-census percentile rank (rankDis/N), and the bracketed-in-time elections additionally carry pcti, the census-night-distance interpolation of the two bracketing censuses' pct — the cross-census comparable quantity (percentiles are; raw scores never are, ABS re-deriving the indexes per census). pcti lanes shipped: 1993/1996/1998 (era CD-cube lanes, derive-division-seifa-stats90s.py), 2004/2007/2010 (whole-unit era-polygon allocations, derive-ced-era-alloc.py) and 2013/2016/2019 (concordance-based). IRSAD lands from the sibling pipeline's irsad-cells.json (derive-irsad.py), which also owns the display store at .build/analysis/seifa-index/irsad-by-division.json. APH lanes carry scores/ranks as PRINTED by the papers; ABS lanes rank from their carried scores. Indexes are re-derived by the ABS per census (PCA weights recomputed), so scores and ranks compare WITHIN a census year, never across them. Census-year and boundary-edition provenance ride each election block (_provenance). APH-lane elections are 1998 (aph98cib04, 1996 census x the 1997-in-force boundaries) and 2004 (aph05cib01, 2001 census x the 2003 edition). 2001 is the ABS's own published 2001-CED cube (scores as printed, ranks computed from them; AEC RR5 att1 prints IRSAD only). 2013-2025 are ABS-cube derivations per 2039.0 (SA1 2011/2016 cubes x their CED allocation for 2013-2019, MB-level 2021 cube x allocation for 2022/2025), exact-verified against the ABS CED SA1-distribution cubes for 2013/2016. 2028 is an irsad-only forward block (2021-census derivation on the 2025 gazetted boundaries; the other three indexes await a census), 1998 an irsd/ier/ieo-only one — IRSAD did not exist until the 2001 census and the five-index-era Advantage composite the paper prints is NOT IRSAD (fixture-only, key `adv`). The statistics-era frames 1993/1996/1998 stay three-index for the same reason: 1993 measures SEIFA 1991 CD scores x the 1993-election division set and 1996 SEIFA 1996 x its set (eraCd* vias, the ABS lane's same 2039.0 sect.2.2 population weighting over the committed era allocations; derive-division-seifa-stats90s.py). Elections before 1993 have no SEIFA coverage. Full map: .build/analysis/seifa-index/rr6-official-seifa-products.md.

pcti90s.title: Between-census percentile interpolation, era lanes (derive-division-seifa-stats90s.py): 1993/1996/1998 the same pcti contract over the SEIFA-91/96/2001 CD cubes and the committed era allocations — three-index era only (no IRSAD before the 2001 census); 1998's pct0 is the measured aph98 paper block read back

_pcti.method: pct = rankDis/N per cell (1/N most disadvantaged … N/N most advantaged); pcti = (1-f)*pct(c0) + f*pct(c1) on the two bracketing censuses' own geometries, f by census-night distance (derive-division-seifa-interp.py and derive-division-seifa-stats90s.py for the era lanes; one side of each election is the measured store row, read back — the c0 side for 1993/1998/2004/2007/2010/2013/2019, the c1 side for 1996/2016)
